meta.name: English
meta.title: Lilo by Kadwood: free, open-source embroidery for everyone
meta.description: Lilo is a free, open-source embroidery app for everyone, from beginners to pros. It turns pictures, drawings and names into stitch files and sends them to your machine. Mac, Windows and Linux.

hero.title: Embroidery for everyone
hero.sub: Lilo is a free, open-source app that turns pictures, drawings and names into embroidery. For Mac, Windows and Linux.
hero.demoCaption: A real sample: the word “Lilo” in a built-in script font, sewn from {stitches} stitches made by Lilo's own engine.
hero.demoAlt: Animation: the word Lilo is traced, then stitched in pink thread

works.sub: Lilo saves the file types your machine reads. Brother and Baby Lock Wi-Fi machines can also get designs straight from Lilo.
works.wifi: Works with Brother Wi-Fi machines (auto-detected). For every other machine: save the file and copy it over with a USB stick.

steps.title: Add a picture
steps.text: Drop in a photo, a drawing, a logo or a name.

steps.title: Lilo makes the stitches
steps.text: Pick your thread colours and size. Watch it sew on screen first.

steps.title: Send it to your machine
steps.text: Over Wi-Fi, or save it to a USB stick. Then press start.

items.a: Yes. Lilo is free now and will stay free, for everyone. There is no trial, no account and no hidden paid part.
Yes. Lilo is for everyone: kids, grandparents, hobby sewers and professionals. If you can drop in a picture, you can make embroidery.
Anyone can read how Lilo is made. Anyone can share it or make it better. Lilo uses the GPL-3 licence.
A sewing machine cannot read a picture. It reads a list of stitches, like a map for the needle. Digitizing turns your picture into that map. Lilo does it for you.

items.q: Will it work with my machine?
items.a: Lilo saves 12 file types, so it fits most home and work machines. Open the full list and look for your brand. Always check your machine manual too, and do a test sew on scrap cloth first.
If your Brother or Baby Lock machine has Wi-Fi, Lilo looks for it on your home network and finds it by itself. No Wi-Fi? Save the file to a USB stick instead.
No. Lilo works offline. It only checks for new versions, and you can turn that off.
Nowhere. They stay on your computer. Lilo never uploads your pictures or your designs.

items.q: Why does Windows show a blue box?
items.a: The Windows installer is not signed yet, so Windows asks you to be careful. Click More info, then Run anyway. The Mac version is signed and checked by Apple.
